newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Regionals hit by post-G7 dollar.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Regionals hit by post-G7 dollar.

text.p: Most regional currencies came under pressure on Monday as the dollar set a three-year high of 1.7395 marks and approached a 56-month high against the yen after the weekend Group of Seven (G7) meeting.
Dealers said the dollar gained ground as the market focused on the failure of the G7 to cite the yen's weakness as a shared concern, as had been widely expected before the meeting.
"The lack of a strong comment from G-7 on the yen decline is pushing up the dollar/majors," said Jimmy Koh, economist at research firm I.D.E.A. in Singapore.

Only the Indonesian rupiah bucked the trend, strengthening against the dollar as players took profit from the U.S. unit's sharp rise last week, which was caused by fears of unrest during the campaign for Indonesia's May 29 general election.
A U.S. bank dealer in Jakarta said the smooth start of the campaign on Sunday had led operators to cash out from dollars.
"I think the dollar is overbought. People are trying to cash out for now," the dealer said, adding that the unloading was also due to month-end factors.
Spot rupiah was quoted at 2,428.5/29.5 at 0420 GMT against an opening of 2,435.5/36.5.
Another foreign bank dealer said dollar buyers wanted to play safe and factor in the start of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) campaign in the country's most populous island of Java on Monday.
He said some people were a bit nervous of the PDI campaign after the minority party split in June last year.
In Malaysia, the ringgit slid through the 2.5100 level against the dollar and dealers said it could head lower, depending on the strength of the dollar/majors.
"I would favour a buy on any dips towards 2.5090/2.5100 and watch the important level of 2.5150," a Singapore-based European bank dealer said.
Koh at I.D.E.A. also said the ringgit was likely to lose more ground over the next few days.
But another European bank dealer said the ringgit's downside would be capped by buying interest from Japanese funds and Malaysian corporates.
He said Bank Negara was rumoured to be constantly checking the market, though it had not come in for the last two weeks.
The Singapore dollar also succumbed to the strength of its U.S. counterpart, but dealers said the U.S. unit continued to face resistance near a previous barrier of 1.4465.
"We have to watch whether the resistance of 1.4465 breaks. If not, there are customers who are long (dollars) and will want to take profit around 1.4465/70," a European bank dealer said.
In Thailand, the Bank of Thailand set the mid-rate at 26.11 baht to the dollar versus 26.08 baht on Friday as the dollar rose against the mark and yen.
The baht was quoted at 26.131/26.134 to the dollar at 0420 GMT against 26.076-26.081 late on Friday.
"The baht seemed to be at the mercy of the dollar in the market which believes the U.S. unit could move higher," said one forex trader in Bangkok.
Dealers said ample money market liquidity was also contributing to the dollar buying.

They said the increased liquidity came from dollar selling in the swap market and money parked in the system by state enterprises, which borrowed funds raised by the government's recent Yankee bond issue in the United States.
-- Madhav Reddy in Kuala Lumpur (603-206 2323), Mantik Kusjanto in Jakarta (6221-384-6364), Anchalee Koetsawang in Bangkok (662-652-0642) and Sonali Desai in Singapore (65-8703090)
